study_identification.title: Linking Personalized Brain Atrophy to Schizophrenia Network and Treatment Response

study_characteristics.study_objective: To test whether personalized brain atrophy maps derived via normative modeling in schizophrenia patients (1) converge to a disorder-specific functional brain network, and (2) explain individual variation in clinical response to repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) treatment.

preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: Quantitative morphometric analysis was performed using FreeSurfer (version 6.0). In brief, images underwent preprocessing steps including intensity normalization, skull stripping, registration into Talairach space, and determination of the gray-white matter boundary and pial surface. CT was computed by measuring the distance between the white matter and pial surfaces at approximately 160,000 vertices. Each subject's reconstructed brain was registered to an average spherical template space and smoothed with an 8 mm full width at half maximum kernel. The entire cortex of each subject was visually inspected, and inaccuracies in segmentation were manually edited. The rs-fMRI data were preprocessed using SPM12 software and AFNI. The processing steps were as follows: (1) delete the first 5 time points, (2) remove temporal spikes more than 2.5 SDs from the mean (AFNI's 3dDespike), (3) slice timing correction, (4) head motion correction, (5) co-registration to the structural image, (6) regress out nuisance regressors (24 head motion parameters, and average signals in the cerebrospinal fluid, white matter, and whole brain), (7) spatial normalization to the MNI space using the matrix produced by structural image segmentation using DARTEL algorithm in SPM12, and (8) spatial smoothing with a 4 mm full width at half maximum Gaussian kernel.

deviation_metric.reason:
Deviation from the normative model is quantified using vertex-wise W-scores, which are z-scores adjusted for age and gender. W-score = (expected - actual) / RSD. Positive W-scores indicate atrophy (CT below normal). Two thresholds were used for defining significant atrophy loci: W>2 (2 SD below normal) and W>2.5. The continuous W-score maps (without thresholding) were used as weighted seeds for atrophy network mapping.

The highest overlapping of personalized atrophy loci was 46% (in the right insular cortex). This overlapping degree dramatically decreased to 29% as the W threshold increased to 2.5. Validation on an independent healthy cohort (n=60) showed high spatial correlation between predicted and actual cortical thickness (r=0.74±0.02, P<.0001). Atrophy loci (W>2) showed moderate spatial overlap (max 46% in right insular cortex at W>2; 29% at W>2.5), indicating heterogeneity. However, functional atrophy networks (derived by correlating W-weighted seed signals with rs-fMRI from 652 HCs) converged to common regions: 88% of patients showed connectivity to bilateral medial prefrontal cortex (MPFC), with 9 clusters exceeding 80% overlap. These atrophy networks were spatially correlated with coordinate-based networks from 27 schizophrenia case-control studies (r=0.67, P_spin<.0001) and distinct from 49 non-psychiatric disorder networks (P_FWE<.001, TFCE-corrected). clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations:
Answer: Yes
Confidence Rating: High
Negative Answer Category: Not Negative
Reason: The authors explicitly discuss four main limitations in the Discussion section: (1) single-center data limiting generalizability, with multicenter modeling proposed as future direction; (2) exclusive focus on schizophrenia, noting that shared pathophysiology across mental disorders warrants future generalization studies; (3) use of inhibitory rTMS (cTBS) only, suggesting opposite effects may occur with excitatory rTMS; (4) methodological caveat that overlap ratios of sparse atrophy maps and dense atrophy networks are not directly comparable.
Supporting Text: Some limitations and future directions should be mentioned. First, the normative modeling was established using data from a single center, and this may not be generalized to other centers. Establishing multicenter modeling will be the next step to integrating normative modeling into clinical practice. Second, this study exclusively focused on schizophrenia patients. An increasing body of evidence implicates shared etiological and pathophysiological characteristics among mental disorders and, thus, it would be interesting for future studies to generalize our findings to other psychiatric disorders. Third, we found that a negative correlation between the rTMS target and atrophy map was associated with poorer symptom improvement. Notably, this result was exclusively based on inhibitory rTMS data. If excitatory rTMS were used, it is possible that the negative correlation of the atrophy map may predict better treatment outcomes. Fourth, we caution that the overlap ratio of the personalized atrophy maps was not comparable to that of the atrophy network maps, because the latter is much less sparse and therefore has higher overlap.

general_notes.general_notes: Methodological details: Smoothing kernels were 8mm FWHM for structural MRI (cortical thickness) and 4mm FWHM for rs-fMRI. HCP-MMP atlas (Glasser et al. 2016, 360 ROIs) was used for spatial correlation analyses. Spin tests (frantisekvasa/rotate_parcellation) with 10,000 permutations were used to correct for spatial autocorrelation, generating null distributions by random cortical ROI rotations. Atrophy network mapping approach: surface W-maps converted to volume space (FreeSurfer mri_surf2vol), W-weighted mean fMRI signal computed, correlated with whole-brain voxels in 652 HC rs-fMRI scans, and group-level one-sample t-tests performed (Fisher z-transformed). Coordinate-based network mapping: 27 case-control contrasts from 21 schizophrenia studies (supplementary table S1) were used to create spherical seeds (3mm diameter, also tested 6mm and 9mm) at reported coordinates, combined per contrast, correlated with 652 HC rs-fMRI, thresholded (t>4.7, P_FWE<.05; also tested t>5.1 and t>5.6), binarized and summed across contrasts. Specificity analysis compared schizophrenia atrophy networks (n=91) to 49 coordinate-based networks from 4 non-psychiatric disorders (AD n=8, FTD n=21, CBS n=12, PNFA n=8; supplementary table S2) using permutation-based two-sample t-tests (FSL PALM, 10,000 permutations, TFCE correction, P_FWE<.001). rTMS protocol: continuous theta-burst stimulation (cTBS) delivered to left TPJ [MNI -51, -31, 23] for 15 days (1800 pulses/day = 3 sessions × 600 pulses with 15-min breaks), 80% resting motor threshold or 50% maximum output, using MagStim Rapid² with 70mm figure-8 coil and Brainsight neuronavigation. Clinical assessments: PANSS (Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale), HAMA (Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale), HAMD (Hamilton Depression Rating Scale). Disease duration: 6.1±4.95 years. Risperidone equivalent dose: 21.6±16.39 mg. Education: 12±2.68 years. Full list of case-control studies for coordinate-based network mapping is in supplementary table S1 (21 studies, 27 contrasts, smoothing kernels ranged 4-12mm). Full list of non-psychiatric disorder studies for specificity analysis is in supplementary table S2 (AD: 8 studies; FTD: 21 studies; CBS: 12 studies; PNFA: 8 studies).
